final.memo:
We have looked at the Company and decided to pass. While the business owns established entertainment franchises, it fails our criteria for a predictable, self-maintaining stream of earnings [D01, D03]. Instead, this is a capital-intensive creative business that requires constant reinvestment to keep its products relevant [D01].

Serious workplace and compensation allegations have created an environment where management credibility is under repair [D05, D07]. In a business where success depends entirely on the retention of creative talent, such cultural instability poses a direct risk of permanent loss of capital [D05].

Furthermore, the record shows a decline in net bookings year-over-year, leaving us uncertain about the sustainability of recent engagement levels [D01, D05]. Given the difficulty of forecasting future performance in such a volatile environment, we are not willing to deploy capital here [D01].

We prefer to hold our cash or invest in businesses we can understand and trust over the long term [D08]. When the clouds gather, we do not try to forecast the weather; we simply stay inside until it is clear [D08].
